newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-LATE PENALTY SAVES DORTMUND AGAINST BOTTOM CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE PENALTY SAVES DORTMUND AGAINST BOTTOM CLUB.

text.p: A late penalty saved European Cup quarter-finalists Borussia Dortmund from an embarrassing draw at bottom club Freiburg in the German first division on Saturday.

With five minutes remaining, injury-hit Dortmund seemed to be heading for a 1-1 draw with Freiburg, who had previously taken just 13 points from 20 games and look doomed to play second division football next season.
But veteran midfielder Michael Zorc's crisp strike from the spot in the 86th minute sealed a 2-1 victory for the defending champions, who replaced Bayern Munich at the top of the Bundesliga.
Dortmund lead on goal difference only and Bayern have a game in hand. The Bavarians travel to Bayer Leverkusen for a fascinating top-of-the-table clash on Sunday.
Dortmund began Saturday's clash without Germany's Euro 96 campaigners Matthias Sammer and Andy Moeller and Swiss striker Stephane Chapuisat.

The champions struggled to make an impact in front of a capacity 22,500 Freiburg crowd. The home side took the lead with a 24th minute goal from Uwe Wassmer before Dortmund's Ghana international Ibrahim Tanko equalised two minutes later.

Borussia, who took a confident step towards the semifinals of the European Cup in midweek with a 3-1 victory over French side Auxerre, then got out of trouble when striker Karlheinz Riedle was brought down in the penalty area.
Zorc stepped up to the spot and silenced the bitterly disappointed Freiburg crowd, who watched their team suffer their seventh consecutive defeat.
"We have always played badly here. Today we still won," Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said. "They put us under pressure in the first half."

VfB Stuttgart, who played the most entertaining football in the league in the first half of the season, moved up to third place after a 4-1 home victory over Hamburg with Brazilian striker Giovane Elber scoring twice.
Bayern go into Sunday's clash with Leverkusen still in shock after their midfielder Dietmar Hamann suffered a stroke at the age of 23 on Thursday evening.

Hamann was taken to hospital after a fall at home when he felt spasms of paralysis on the left side of his body. Doctors said on Saturday the player's condition had stabilised and he would be able to play football again.
But Bayern's striker and national team captain Juergen Klinsmann said: "We have all been very worried about Didi. It's been a big shock."
